kind: single saved-state instrumented feature cost profile; development diagnosis, not strength or CG deadline evidence

protocol.kind: fixed saved-state V3 feature cost profile; no games or strategy edits
protocol.selection: all 40 pinned arena games, turns 0..19, one pass, one V3 call per state
protocol.memory: actual public board prefix and previous accepted recorded disruption restored each turn
protocol.rng: same explicit per-state seed as NeuralSavedStateBudgetProbe; not arena RNG reconstruction
protocol.timing: inclusive nested nanoTime and per-thread allocated-byte deltas; overhead included in parents
limits: Diagnostic instrumentation changes code/JIT and adds method/native calls.
One local sample per state, no repeated timing trials and no CG CPU/runtime reconstruction.
Allocation counters show allocated bytes, not retained memory or pause causality.
All states are reused development evidence; no strength or outcome claims.
Actions compared with prior ample-budget probe under the identical seed/memory convention.

warmup.method: one disposable V3 on the same largest saved map; 36-ms slices, unchanged board

findings: Direct feature Dijkstra dominates measured time: 49.32% of all play and 58.89% of large-map play; active-route Dijkstra is additional.
completionGain consumes 14.75% of all play and 16.15% of large-map play; its updateConnections dominates that subtotal.
completionGain.updateConnections allocates 27.39 MB, 90.2% of total per-play allocations; large-map share is about 95.0%.
copyFrom alone costs under 1% of play, so eliminating copies without the connection reconstruction is unlikely to materially improve time.
An exact direct-income computation would target most allocations but only around one sixth of measured play time before secondary effects.
A per-source Dijkstra tree cache within each unchanged prepare board may target repeated pair destinations; exact path ties and blocked masks require separate validation.
All 800 actions equal the earlier uninstrumented ample-budget probe; actual replay prefix scores/paint/cells remained exact.
limitations: Nested metrics are inclusive; never add completionGain to its children or activePairRoutes to its Dijkstra child.
Instrumentation adds clock/allocation-native calls and changes JIT decisions; percentages are local diagnostic estimates, not uninstrumented speedup guarantees.
Per-thread allocations measure bytes allocated during bot.play; initialization, copied replay input and result reporting are excluded.
The same previously selected 800 positions are reused; this does not establish strength or explain CG underpainting causally.
One fixed pass and one disposable 500-ms warm-up; no retries or selected fastest runs.
